metadata.title: The rules of discovery
metadata.ordering: First dated mapped governance record, including prior treaty obligations. Dates are selected anchors, not the first governance worldwide.
metadata.coverage: Fifteen selected UK, US and international cases. Tracks are UK/GB, US and international; sources define territorial and activity limits. No scientific milestone establishes policy effectiveness.
metadata.colour_rule: Solid blue: mapped law or legal framework family. Dashed blue: funding conditions. Green: nonbinding guidance, including government, intergovernmental, professional and industry guidance. Outlined continuation: continuity not fully established. Red hatching: a specified restriction, not a field-wide shutdown. Grey: no specialist framework mapped, not absence of law. Dash-dot blue identifies a general legal framework applied to the activity.
metadata.origin_rule: Starting anchors are selected proposals, achievements, meetings or practices. They do not establish a unique discovery date. Earlier dated events appear as left-pointing labels.
metadata.date_rule: Day, month and year precision are stored separately. Month/year-only markers use the midpoint of the stated period for layout, not an invented event date.
metadata.cutoff_rule: Open arrows indicate continuation without a verified end. Solid coverage is limited to sourced framework scope; uncertainty is visible. The chart ends at the review cutoff, not a policy end date.
metadata.general_duties: General law, consent duties and professional ethics may apply before specialist frameworks. UK/GB tracks do not imply identical territorial coverage.
metadata.source_rule: Reading depth is recorded per source. Retained sources not re-read are explicitly identified. No claim of comprehensive full-text legal review is made.
metadata.restriction_rule: Red strips are selected restrictions, not an exhaustive list of legal prohibitions. No red strip does not mean unrestricted activity. Strip height is not a fraction of the field.
metadata.success_rule: Achievement markers identify reported scientific or clinical milestones. They do not establish policy effectiveness or universal treatment safety.
metadata.presentation: Descriptive history of scientific milestones, concerns, debates and governance responses across UK, US and international settings. Compact editorial style with centred markers. Sequence alone does not establish causation.
